findings.title: Format the load_reporting_interval validation error
findings.trigger: The first LoadStatsResponse carries a load_reporting_interval that CheckValid() rejects.
findings.impact: The returned error reads `invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>` because it formats the outer `err`, which is already nil after `stream.Recv()` succeeded. The base code formatted the ptypes.Duration error here, so the validation cause is now dropped. Rejection behavior is unchanged.

questions.title: Are the remaining github.com/golang/protobuf imports out of scope?
questions.evidence: The supplied spec says the change migrates protobuf imports across the repository. Non-test files on review-head still import github.com/golang/protobuf: channelz/service/service.go:26-27 and channelz/service/func_linux.go:24-25 (commit f58f647 reverts the channelz changes), credentials/credentials.go:31, xds/internal/xdsclient/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:32 (jsonpb), and reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go:41. internal/pretty/pretty.go:27 keeps the v1 bridge deliberately.
questions.why_it_matters: If the migration is meant to be complete, these are unmet acceptance requirements and the change needs a must-fix requirement finding. If the scope is intentional, nothing in this change is missing.
questions.answer: The change author or maintainer states whether these files are in scope for this change or deferred to a later change.

observations.fact: test/tools/go.mod lowers golang.org/x/tools from v0.17.0 on main to v0.14.0 and adds golang.org/x/sys v0.13.0; no commit message in the range explains the tooling downgrade.
status.Details() now reports an Any with an empty type URL as `invalid empty type URL` where main reported `message type url "" is invalid`; status/status_test.go pins the new text.

requirements.evidence: The migration is done in most non-test code, but six non-test files still import github.com/golang/protobuf (see the question migration/remaining-legacy-imports). internal/pretty/pretty.go keeps the v1 bridge for MessageV2.
